# Vault Tokens & Contract Addresses

Repository of Contract for Umami's GM Vaults

Deposits in Umami's GM Vaults are represented by tokens implemented using the ERC-4626 standard for each respective vault. If the respective Vault generates a profit, PPS (Price Per Share) of your token will increase in relation to the underlying token of your Vault. Each individual Vault is represented by specific tokens.

sourceSemantics.rootDeposit: rootEvidence.sources["src/vaults/AssetVault.sol"].content decoded lines105-121: nonzero preview, capacity, caller USDC transfer under existing allowance, payable fixed aggregate handleDeposit with selected callback. Zero forwarded at argument3.
sourceSemantics.rootRedeem: Same root source lines132-154: positive shares, estimated assets, existing owner-to-caller allowance consumption when different, external self-call transferFrom under owner-to-AssetVault allowance, payable fixed aggregate handleWithdraw. Zero forwarded at argument4.
sourceSemantics.redemptionDifference: Ordinary redeem decoded line80 requires assets <= aggregate USDC balance. redeemWithCallback lines132-154 omits it; zero callback does not restore this local liquidity precheck.
sourceSemantics.existingAllowance: Root lines439-442 consumes owner-to-caller share allowance. Retained solmate ERC20.transferFrom source consumes allowance[from][msg.sender] for the external self-call; msg.sender is the AssetVault, requiring owner-to-AssetVault allowance.
sourceSemantics.asynchronousContext: Contextual AggregateVault lines97-144 stores requests, computes gas requirement by callback!=zero, forwards all ETH to rebalanceKeeper and runs configured deposit/withdraw hooks. Contextual AggregateVaultStorage lines465-485 stores callback alongside sender/receiver/vault/amount/minimum/block. This does not bind the current configured aggregate implementation.
sourceSemantics.funding: USDC principal from caller existing allowance; owner shares from owner existing allowances. Payable ETH funds execution fees. Returned shares/assets are estimates, not completed settlement. No live funded execution or identity claim.

limitations: Static exact-root source/ABI observation only, not live runtime identity, current configuration, funded execution, liquidity, settlement, complete workflow or financial-safety assurance. Independent grants, pauses, canonical calldata bounds and final acceptance remain mandatory.

Only Arbitrum42161 gmUSDC BTC-backed AssetVault 0x5f851f67d24419982ecd7b7765defd64fbb50a97 is admitted. Maintained GM deployment evidence does not admit deprecated GLP products or any other Umami root. Retained configuration identifies native USDC 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831,6 decimals; vault shares also have6 decimals.

Mandatory umami-zero-request-callback-v1 requires the selected callback address to be exactly zero. This disables only the user-selected request callback; configured protocol hooks, token behavior and asynchronous keepers remain. No new permit, allowance, operator, role, delegation or presign installation is admitted; no multicall child composition is added.

Payable native ETH is keeper execution-fee funding, not USDC principal. Exact root forwards all msg.value to its configured aggregate. Contextual aggregate source requires configured gas times tx.gasprice and forwards all supplied value to rebalanceKeeper without an excess refund here. No fixed fee quote or zero-native-value restriction is imposed.

minOutAfterFees is forwarded, not locally enforced by the AssetVault; contextual aggregate source stores it for deferred handling. No caller deadline or immediate settlement/min-output guarantee. Rounding, dynamic fees, pauses, keeper/oracle execution, hooks, buffers and rebalancing may affect acceptance and outcomes.

Escrows owner shares via an external ERC20 self-call. Existing owner-to-AssetVault share allowance is required even when owner equals caller; caller different from owner additionally consumes existing owner-to-caller share allowance. No permission is installed. Receiver chooses settlement destination; cancellation uses recorded initiating sender, not necessarily owner or receiver.

Callback argument4 (zero-based) must be zero. Positive shares and nonzero preview assets are checked on chain; returned assets are an estimate, not an immediate underlying payout. Unlike ordinary redeem, redeemWithCallback omits the local aggregate-USDC-balance precheck even at zero callback, so no equivalent immediate-liquidity rejection is claimed. Acceptance and deferred settlement still depend on fixed configured protocol machinery.

Static exact-deployment ABI/source inventory only; no runtime identity, execution, liquidity, funding, complete-workflow or financial-safety assurance. Independent grants, pause checks and canonical-calldata controls remain mandatory.

Only Arbitrum gmUSDC BTC-backed vault 0x5f851F67D24419982EcD7b7765deFD64fBb50a97 is selected, not old GLP vaults or the ETH-backed gmUSDC whose deposit pause was observed. Underlying is 6-decimal native USDC 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831, not bridged USDC.e; vault shares also have 6 decimals.

Deposit transfers caller USDC into this vault using allowance to this vault, then forwards a request to its configured aggregate vault. Receiver is explicit; zero is rejected in the bundled aggregate source. The immediate return value is an estimate, not minted-share or settlement confirmation. No standalone prefunding is admitted.

Redeem escrows owner shares in this vault rather than immediately burning/paying them. Owner must approve the vault to transfer shares even when owner equals caller; a different caller additionally consumes owner-to-caller share allowance. Receiver controls settlement destination, whereas cancellation refunds the recorded initiating sender, not necessarily owner or receiver.

Both deposit and redeem are payable because msg.value is forwarded to the aggregate for keeper execution gas, not ETH principal. Bundled aggregate code requires msg.value >= configured gas requirement times tx.gasprice and forwards all supplied value to rebalanceKeeper, without an excess refund in these entrypoints; documented approximately 0.001 ETH is not a fixed fee quote.

minOutAfterFees is forwarded into the pending request without local enforcement. Bundled aggregate source stores it for deferred execution; current exact aggregate/request-handler source and minimum-enforcement implementation were not independently bound, and no live execution/min-output guarantee is asserted. No caller deadline is present.

Conversions floor at the share price and dynamic fees can consume small inputs; deposit requires nonzero preview shares and capacity, ordinary redeem requires nonzero preview assets and sufficient aggregate USDC before it can even queue. The separately scoped redeemWithCallback still requires nonzero preview assets but omits that local aggregate-balance precheck, even at zero callback; no equivalent immediate-liquidity rejection is asserted. Documented fees are 2% annual management and 20% yield plus dynamic entry/exit fees; actual configured execution-time rates may differ.

Requests depend on keeper/oracle execution, configured hooks, buffers and rebalancing; no fixed settlement delay or payout guarantee. cancelRequest checks exact vault and initiating sender, returns escrowed USDC or shares and clears the pending request; already cleared/executed or unavailable escrow requests can revert, and keeper ETH is not refunded by this function.

Explorer snapshot reports depositPaused=false, withdrawalPaused=false, aggregateVault=0x1E914730B4Cd343aE14530F0BBF6b350d83B833d and asset=USDC. These are point-in-time reported values, not persistence or runtime attestation. Configurator can pause operations or replace aggregateVault; the immutable AUTH reference is not automatically replaced with it.

Nonzero caller-selected request callbacks remain excluded. The two separately granted callback entrypoints are admitted only under mandatory zero-request-callback scope at this exact root; zero disables neither configured protocol hooks nor asynchronous keepers. Permit, approvals/transfers, privileged share accounting, pause/configuration and all views remain excluded. The fixed configured aggregate dependency may revert or change; its source bundled in the vault compilation is contextual only, not an independently verified current deployed aggregate ABI. Umami requires lawful jurisdictional participation; no KYC eligibility or legal suitability is inferred.
